about.title: Emeryville Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Emeryville is a small city, but its clinics, urgent care centers, and nearby hospital systems serve a much larger daily population thanks to the businesses and residents packed into this Alameda County community. When a diagnosis is missed, a surgery goes wrong, or a medication error causes harm, the aftermath can be confusing and isolating. California law puts strict, specific rules around these cases — deadlines that move faster than most people expect, notice requirements before a lawsuit can even be filed, and a requirement for qualified medical expert review. LawProactive doesn't practice law or take a cut of any settlement; we simply listen to what happened, ask a few questions, and connect eligible callers with an independent attorney in our network who handles medical malpractice matters in Alameda County. There's no cost to talk with someone and no pressure to move forward. If you're trying to figure out whether what happened to you in Emeryville crosses the line from a bad outcome into malpractice, a conversation with an attorney is the way to find out.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Through LawProactive

items.title: California's Clock Moves Fast
items.desc: Under MICRA, claims generally must be brought within one year of discovering the injury and no more than three years from when it occurred, plus a 90-day pre-suit notice requirement. Waiting even a few weeks to ask questions can quietly narrow your options.

items.title: Expert Review Is Usually Required
items.desc: California law almost always requires a qualified medical expert to support a malpractice claim — this isn't something you can put together on your own. An attorney in our network can help arrange that kind of review before deciding whether to move forward.

items.title: No Upfront Cost, No Guarantee of a Result
items.desc: Attorneys in the LawProactive network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. We can't promise an outcome — a poor result from treatment isn't automatically malpractice — but a conversation costs nothing.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after treatment in Emeryville — is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law is clear that a bad medical outcome alone doesn't mean malpractice occurred; there has to be a deviation from the accepted standard of care that caused harm. An independent attorney, usually working with a qualified medical expert, can help evaluate whether your situation meets that bar.

items.question: How much time do I have to bring a claim?
items.answer: Under MICRA, the general rule is one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, and no more than three years from the date it happened. There's also a 90-day notice period required before filing suit, so it's best to start the conversation sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does LawProactive handle malpractice claims for Emeryville hospitals directly?
items.answer: No — LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, so we don't handle or litigate claims ourselves. We connect people in Emeryville and elsewhere in Alameda County with independent attorneys who focus on medical malpractice and can evaluate the specifics of your care.
